chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭalḥah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a thief who entered upon a woman to steal her belongings. When he had gathered the clothes, his soul prompted him further, so he overpowered her regarding herself and had intercourse with her. Then her son stirred, so he got up and killed him with an axe that he had with him. When he finished, he carried the clothes and went to leave, but she attacked him with the axe and killed him. Then his family came the next day demanding blood-compensation for him.

So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Judge in this case as I have described to you.” Then he said: “His masters/heirs, those who demanded blood for him, are liable for the blood-money of the boy; and the thief is liable, from what he left behind, for four thousand dirhams for his having overpowered her sexually. He is a fornicator, and this is a financial penalty against his property. And there is nothing against her for her killing him, because he was a thief.”

key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: the boy; the woman’s son who was killed
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirham; the monetary unit used for the assessed compensation
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money; financial compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.زَانٍ: fornicator; the legal characterization given in the ruling
key_terms.سَارِقٍ: a thief; the criminal intruder whose actions are the subject of the ruling
key_terms.غَرَامَةٌ: financial penalty or liability imposed upon property
key_terms.فَكَابَرَهَا: he overpowered her by force; indicating coercive sexual violation
key_terms.فَوَاقَعَهَا: he had intercourse with her; referring here to forced intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام on a thief who sexually assaults a woman, kills her son, and is then killed by the woman?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling from Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام concerning a case involving theft, sexual assault, homicide, and retaliatory killing. It establishes financial liability for the killing of the boy and for the sexual violation, while ruling that the woman bears no liability for killing the thief in these circumstances.
